Subject: Phased tenor sync & staged onramp proposal (Brightwell)

Elaine / Samir,

Great talking yesterday — thanks for walking me through the platform rollout timelines and the three pilot clinics you plan to onboard in Q2. As discussed, attached is a short proposal that lets Brightwell align renewal boundaries across existing subscriptions while providing a staged GPU capacity onramp to cover pilot → regional rollouts. High level: 

- Term: 36 months (co-term with existing enterprise contract on 2029-01-01)
- Onramp: 6-month pilot tranche (30% committed), then 18-month scale tranche (70% committed), final 12-month steady state with optional burst credits
- Auto-renew: Opt-in with 90-day notice and true-up reporting each quarter
- Price: blended per-token rate that steps down at tranche boundaries; see attached PDF for examples and net present value of credits

Why this structure: it gives predictable unit economics while ensuring you only pay for the capacity profile you consume as you scale clinics. We also include a short SLA carveout for pilot latency targets and an emergency burst lane for operational incidents.

Attachments: Brightwell_Phased_Onramp_Proposal_RWI-2937.pdf, SOW_Term_Schedule_v2.xlsx

Ask: can you confirm procurement cadence and whether co-terming with your existing 2029 renewal date works, or would you prefer a 24- or 12‑month option instead? If co-term is acceptable we can prepare a single amendment + SOW and aim for a DocuSign send by Feb 24.

Thanks — I copied Marissa for commercial terms and Camila for the ops/onboarding plan so we have all stakeholders looped.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Rafael — thanks for the clear plan and the docs. Quick notes from our side: 

1) Procurement: we'll need a 30‑day review window from legal & procurement. procurement@brightwell.io is copied.
2) Co-term: co-terming to 2029-01-01 is preferred (keeps our vendor calendar simple).
3) Pilot tranche: finance needs the first‑year cashflow profile (monthly phasing) and the ability to true up monthly rather than quarterly if usage is volatile. Is monthly true‑up feasible?
4) Pricing: is there a floor for per‑token discounts if we accelerate clinic rollouts (i.e., if we hit 10 clinics by month 9)?

I'll get Samir to pull together the clinic start timelines. If you can get an updated SOW with monthly true‑up examples and the accelerated-rollout ladder, procurement can start review on Monday (2/15).

— Elaine

Thanks Elaine — great, that's helpful. Answers inline: 

1) Monthly true‑up: yes — we can support monthly reporting and true‑up for the pilot and scale tranches. We'll include an optional monthly-billed pilot schedule in the SOW (see attached SOW_Term_Schedule_v2.xlsx).
2) Accelerated-rollout ladder: we can add an automatic discount tier if you hit +10 clinics by month 9 (5% additional on blended per-token). That would be retroactive to the month you hit the threshold.
3) Legal/procurement: understood — we'll target sending a redline-ready amendment + SOW by 2/18 so your team has the 30‑day review window. DocuSign link will be provided once we agree on final numbers.

Operational note (Camila): Camila, can you confirm the onboarding lead times and whether we should pre-allocate a warm GPU pool for the pilot clinics?

Next step: I'll update the SOW with monthly true-up columns and the rollout-ladder and push an internal commercial summary to Marissa for signoff by EOD 2/16.

Best,

Rafael / Camila — reviewed the updated commercial draft. A couple of commercial clarifications before we send to procurement: 

- Early-acceleration credit: instead of a 5% retroactive discount, propose a one‑time credit equal to 10% of the incremental tokens consumed in the month the +10 clinic threshold is hit. This simplifies billing and accounting for both parties.
- Minimum floor: keep a 12‑month committed minimum in the 36‑month term for accounting; that is, if they terminate early, the remaining committed value for the first 12 months is due. The rest is tiered true‑ups (we can keep the opt‑out language for extraordinary circumstances).
- Billing cadence: due to Brightwell cashflow preference, offer monthly invoicing for the pilot tranche and quarterly invoicing thereafter (with reconciliation).

If Brightwell is okay with the credit approach and the 12‑month floor we can finalize the amendment and SOW. Rafael — I'll prepare the commercial summary and an example invoice cadence to include in the packet.

Marissa Cole

Elaine / team — operational confirmation: 

- Warm GPU pool: we recommend pre‑allocating a small warm pool for the 6‑month pilot (2x V100-equivalent instances reserved) to ensure predictable latency for initial clinics. This will be billed as part of the pilot tranche and clearly shown as a line item in the SOW.
- Onboarding timeline: once SOW signed, onboarding kickoff within 10 business days; clinic-by-clinic enablement cadence in SOW enables one clinic per week after kickoff (staggered).
- Support SLA: we'll include a 24/7 incident line for the first 90 days of the pilot and a 4‑hour P1 response SLA.

Elaine — glad to hear procurement will start review on 2/15. Rafael — if procurement requests a single amendment that includes the billing cadence table, the warm pool line, and the early-acceleration credit approach, we should be able to send for signature by 2/22.
